claim: The deamidase OspI from enteric bacteria Shigella flexneri deamidates a glutamine residue in the host ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme UBC13 and converts it to glutamate (Q100E).
source: The deamidase OspI from enteric bacteria Shigella flexneri deamidates a glutamine residue in the host ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme UBC13 and converts it to glutamate (Q100E).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Sanada et al., 2012) as stated in the Introduction section.

claim: Deamidation of UBC13 silences its polyubiquitination activity in complex with the RING-finger ubiquitin ligase TRAF6 and the downstream NF-κB inflammatory response.
source: Consequently, its polyubiquitination activity in complex with the RING-finger ubiquitin ligase TRAF6 and the downstream NF-κB inflammatory response is silenced.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Sanada et al., 2012) and experimental data shown in Figure 1A and B.

claim: Deamidation inhibits the interaction between UBC13 and TRAF6 RING-domain (TRAF6RING) by perturbing both the native and transient interactions.
source: We report that deamidation inhibits the interaction between UBC13 and TRAF6 RING-domain (TRAF6RING) by perturbing both the native and transient interactions.
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR titration data (Figure 1D-I), MD simulations (Figures 2-8), and binding assays throughout the manuscript.

claim: Deamidation creates a new intramolecular salt-bridge in UBC13 that competes with a critical intermolecular salt-bridge at the native UBC13/TRAF6RING interface.
source: Deamidation creates a new intramolecular salt-bridge in UBC13 that competes with a critical intermolecular salt-bridge at the native UBC13/TRAF6RING interface.
evidence: This claim is supported by MD simulation data showing R14/E100 salt-bridge formation (Figure 2B) and NMR data showing R14 sidechain perturbations (Figure 2C-G).

claim: The salt-bridge competition prevents transient interactions necessary to form a typical UBC13/RING complex.
source: Moreover, the salt-bridge competition prevents transient interactions necessary to form a typical UBC13/RING complex.
evidence: This claim is supported by unbiased association MD simulations (Figures 7-8) and transient complex theory calculations (Table 3).

claim: Repulsion between E100 and the negatively charged surface of RING prevents transient interactions in the UBC13/RING complex.
source: Repulsion between E100 and the negatively charged surface of RING also prevents transient interactions in the UBC13/RING complex.
evidence: This claim is supported by transient complex theory calculations (Table 3), US simulations (Figure 6), and electrostatic surface potential analysis (Figure 3A).

claim: dUBC13 has reduced polyubiquitination activity compared to UBC13 when complexed with TRAF6RZ3.
source: dUBC13 had reduced polyubiquitination activity than UBC13, either with longer TRAF6RZ3 or with shorter TRAF6RING (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This claim is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: dUBC13 has reduced polyubiquitination activity compared to UBC13 when complexed with TRAF6RING.
source: dUBC13 had reduced polyubiquitination activity than UBC13, either with longer TRAF6RZ3 or with shorter TRAF6RING (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This claim is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The E2 activity of UBC13 is not altered upon deamidation.
source: However, a comparison of the extent of polyubiquitination by the UBC13/MMS2 heterodimer in the absence of E3 was similar between UBC13 and dUBC13, indicating that E2 activity is not altered upon deamidation (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C comparing UBC13 and dUBC13 activity without E3.

claim: The dissociation constant (Kd) of UBC13/TRAF6RING interaction is 0.39 (±0.04) mM.
source: The peak shifts in UBC13 titration spectra were fitted to yield a Kd of 0.39 (±0.04) mM (Figure 1I and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR titration data and fitting analysis shown in Figure 1I and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Deamidation does not change the fold of UBC13.
source: The absence of major CSPs in the rest of dUBC13 indicated that deamidation did not change the fold of UBC13.
evidence: This claim is supported by chemical shift perturbation analysis (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) and secondary structure prediction (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).

claim: The secondary structure of UBC13 is unperturbed upon deamidation.
source: Moreover, analysis of the backbone and Cβ chemical shifts in dUBC13 confirmed that the secondary structure was unperturbed (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR chemical shift analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: TRAF6RING does not bind dUBC13 at physiological concentrations.
source: Negligible peak shifts were detected in dUBC13 even when the TRAF6RING was titrated up to 6-fold higher than dUBC13, indicating that TRAF6RING does not bind dUBC13 (Figure 1E–H).
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR titration data shown in Figure 1E-H and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: The estimated Kd of dUBC13/TRAF6RING interaction is 6.34 (±2.6) mM.
source: A rough estimate of the Kd was obtained by comparing the CSPs at the UBC13 interface at the same protein: ligand concentration between UBC13 and dUBC13, which suggested the Kd of 6.34 (±2.6) mM.
evidence: This claim is based on comparison of chemical shift perturbations between UBC13 and dUBC13 at equivalent protein:ligand ratios.

claim: Substitution of Q100 with a neutral amino acid (Q100A) does not significantly affect the affinity of the UBC13/TRAF6RING complex.
source: If the reduced affinity is precisely due to the negative charge at residue 100, then substitution of Q100 with a neutral amino acid should not affect the affinity of the complex. TRAF6RING was titrated to Q100A-UBC13, and the measured Kd was 0.54 (±0.07) mM (Figure 1I), which is similar to UBC13/TRAF6RING.
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR titration data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: Substitution of Q100 with aspartate (Q100D) significantly reduces the affinity of the UBC13/TRAF6RING complex.
source: However, when Q100 was substituted with another acidic residue aspartate (D), the affinity dropped significantly (Kd ~4.6 (±1.8)) mM, Figure 1I), confirming that substitution at Q100 with a negatively charged residue inhibited the interaction between UBC13 and TRAF6RING.
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR titration data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: Q100 does not form any direct contact with TRAF6RING in the native complex structure.
source: In the UBC13/TRAF6RING native complex structure, Q100 does not form any direct contact with TRAF6RING (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is based on structural analysis of the crystal structure (PDB 3HCU) shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The UBC13 interface is positively charged while the TRAF6RING interface is negatively charged.
source: The UBC13 interface was positively charged, while the TRAF6RING was negatively charged.
evidence: This claim is supported by electrostatic surface potential calculations shown in Figure 3A.

claim: An intramolecular R14/E100 salt-bridge forms in dUBC13 with 48% occupancy in MD simulations.
source: The distance between R14-Cζ and E100-Cδ atoms against time in the conventional MD simulation of dUBC13 is given (top). The presence/absence of a salt-bridge based on a 0.5 nm cutoff value are digitized to a Markov chain, where the presence of a salt-bridge is one and absence is 0. The occupancy of the R14/E100 salt-bridge is 48%.
evidence: This claim is supported by MD simulation data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: R14 sidechain conformation is perturbed upon deamidation as shown by NMR.
source: 15N-edited HSQCs of the Arginine Nε-Hε groups were collected for both UBC13 and dUBC13, which showed shifted resonances for the arginine sidechains (R7, R14, and R102) around residue E100, indicating that these sidechain conformations are perturbed (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR spectroscopy data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: R14 forms a new intramolecular salt-bridge in dUBC13 as evidenced by two separate resonances for R14 Nη atoms in 15Nε/η-13Cζ correlation spectra.
source: The R14 Nη atoms had two separate resonances in dUBC13 but not UBC13 (Figure 2F, expanded in 2G), implying that R14 forms a new intramolecular salt-bridge in dUBC13, consistent with the MD simulations.
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR spectroscopy data shown in Figure 2F and 2G.

claim: R14 forms an intermolecular salt-bridge with E69 of TRAF6RING at the interface of the native complex.
source: At the interface of UBC13/TRAF6RING, R14 of UBC13 forms an intermolecular salt-bridge with E69 of TRAF6RING (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is based on structural analysis of the crystal structure shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The wild type UBC13/TRAF6RING complex is stable throughout a 200 ns MD simulation trajectory.
source: The wt complex was stable throughout the 200 ns trajectory with low rmsd (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by MD simulation data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The deamidated UBC13/TRAF6RING complex is unstable for a significant duration (75 ns) in MD simulations.
source: The deamidated complex was unstable for a significant duration of 75 ns, wherein the rmsd of TRAF6RING increased substantially (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by MD simulation data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The R14/E69 intermolecular salt-bridge disrupts and the R14/E100 intramolecular salt-bridge forms concurrently in the dUBC13 complex during MD simulations.
source: However, concurrent to the high rmsd in dUBC13 complex, the R14/E69 intermolecular salt-bridge disrupted and the R14/E100 intramolecular salt-bridge formed, suggesting that salt-bridge competition might destabilize the native dUBC13 complex (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B, Video 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by MD simulation data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B and Video 1.

claim: The occupancy of the R14/E69 intermolecular salt-bridge drops from 99% in the wild type complex to 40% in the dUBC13 complex.
source: The occupancy of the R14/E69 intermolecular salt-bridge dropped from 99% in the wt complex to 40% in the dUBC13 complex (Supplementary file 1-table S1).
evidence: This claim is supported by MD simulation analysis provided in Supplementary file 1-table S1.

claim: The ΔGPMF of the dUBC13/TRAF6RING complex is −0.67 (±0.50) kcal/mol.
source: In contrast, ΔGPMF of dUBC13 complex gradually reduced by only 0.7 kcal/mol, suggesting that deamidation reduces the stability of the complex.
evidence: This claim is supported by Umbrella Sampling MD simulations shown in Table 1.

claim: The difference in ΔGPMF between the deamidated and wild type complex (ΔΔGPMF) is 1.37 kcal/mol.
source: The difference in ΔGPMF between the deamidated and wt complex , ΔΔGPMF = 1.37 kcal/mol was of the same order as the decrease in binding energy observed by NMR titrations, ΔΔG = 1.69 kcal/mol (Figure 1I).
evidence: This claim is derived from the ΔGPMF values in Table 1 and compared to experimental NMR data.

claim: The ΔGPMF of Q100A-UBC13/TRAF6RING complex is similar to the wild type complex.
source: The ΔGPMF of Q100A-UBC13/TRAF6RING is similar to the wt complex (Table 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by Umbrella Sampling MD simulations shown in Table 1.

claim: The mean Coulombic Interaction Energy (CIE) is significantly higher in the dUBC13 complex compared to wild type.
source: The mean CIE was significantly higher in dUBC13 complex, suggesting that deamidation primarily inhibited electrostatic interactions (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by CIE analysis from US simulations shown in Figure 3F.

claim: R14-mediated interactions are essential for the binding of UBC13 to TRAF6RING.
source: Interestingly, when the US simulations were repeated with R14A-UBC13, the ΔGPMF was insignificant, indicating that R14-mediated interactions are essential for the binding (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by Umbrella Sampling MD simulations shown in Figure 3B and Table 1.

claim: Less force and work are required to dissociate the dUBC13/TRAF6RING complex compared to the wild type complex in Steered MD simulations.
source: Compared to the wt complex, less force and work were required to dissociate the dUBC13 complex, indicating reduced stability due to deamidation (Figure 4A–C, Table 2 and Supplementary file 1-table S3).
evidence: This claim is supported by Steered MD simulation data shown in Figure 4A-C and Table 2.

claim: The intramolecular R14/E100 salt-bridge competes with the intermolecular R14/E69 salt-bridge during dissociation in Steered MD simulations.
source: As TRAF6RING starts to dissociate, the intramolecular R14/E100 salt-bridge competes with the intermolecular R14/E69 salt-bridge and reduces its strength (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplements 1–2 and Supplementary file 1-table S4).
evidence: This claim is supported by Steered MD simulation data shown in Figure 4D and supplementary figures.

claim: The R14/E69 intermolecular salt-bridge persists until complete dissociation in the wild type complex during Steered MD.
source: In the wt complex, whereas the other contacts disrupted early, the R14/E69 intermolecular salt-bridge persisted till the complex dissociated completely (Figure 5A–5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by Steered MD simulation data shown in Figure 5A-C and Video 2.

claim: In the dUBC13 complex, the R14/E69 intermolecular salt-bridge disrupts prematurely and the R14/E100 intramolecular salt-bridge forms simultaneously during Steered MD.
source: However, in the trajectory of the dUBC13 complex, the intermolecular salt-bridge disrupted prematurely, and the intramolecular salt-bridge formed simultaneously (Figure 5D–5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by Steered MD simulation data shown in Figure 5D-F and Video 3.

claim: The association rate constant of the wild type UBC13/TRAF6RING complex reduces at high salt compared to low salt.
source: The association rate constant of the wt complex reduced at high salt compared to low salt, confirming that electrostatic interactions are important for the association of wt transient complex (Table 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by transient complex theory calculations shown in Table 3.

claim: The association rate constant reduces by three-fold for dUBC13/TRAF6RING at low salt compared to wild type.
source: The association rate constant reduced by three-fold for dUBC13/TRAF6RING at low salt, indicating that deamidation reduces the association of the transient complex.
evidence: This claim is supported by transient complex theory calculations shown in Table 3.

claim: Electrostatic repulsion between E100 and the negatively charged interface of TRAF6RING destabilizes transient complexes.
source: The repulsive interaction probably destabilized the attractive interaction, and it disrupted soon after. The complex dissociated subsequently (Figure 6B). The instability of deamidated complex was also evident in other US windows (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B–E). Overall, electrostatic repulsion between E100 and the negatively charged interface of TRAF6RING was observed in the dUBC13 transient complexes, which could destabilize it.
evidence: This claim is supported by US simulation data shown in Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Native-like association of the wild type complex is 3-fold higher at low salt than high salt in unbiased-association simulations.
source: Similar to Transcomp calculations (Table 3), the native-like association of the wt complex was 3-fold higher at low salt than high salt, confirming that formation of the transient complex was dependent on the long-range electrostatic interactions.
evidence: This claim is supported by unbiased-association MD simulation data shown in Table 4.

claim: The association and stability of native-like transient complexes drop by 2.3 fold in the dUBC13 complex at low salt.
source: The association and stability dropped by 2.3 fold in the dUBC13 complex at low salt, suggesting that deamidation reduces the formation of the native-like transient complex.
evidence: This claim is supported by unbiased-association MD simulation data shown in Table 4.

claim: The positions of TRAF6RING are tightly clustered around the UBC13 binding interface in wild type association simulations.
source: The distribution of TRAF6RING positions around the helix 1 of UBC13 indicates that the TRAF6RING positions are tightly clustered around the UBC13 binding interface (Figure 7A).
evidence: This claim is supported by unbiased-association MD simulation analysis shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The positions of TRAF6RING are dispersed when it interacts with dUBC13 in association simulations.
source: The positions of TRAF6RING are dispersed when it interacts with dUBC13, and none of the clusters coincide with the native complex (Figure 7B).
evidence: This claim is supported by unbiased-association MD simulation analysis shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Several TRAF6RING clusters around R14 are absent in the dUBC13 complex.
source: Several TRAF6RING clusters around R14 were absent in the dUBC13 complex, indicating that the transient contacts between R14 and TRAF6RING are absent in dUBC13 (Figure 7C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by unbiased-association MD simulation analysis shown in Figure 7C and D.

claim: The Kd of E69A-TRAF6RING with UBC13 is 1.51 (±0.68) mM.
source: When 15N-UBC13 was titrated with E69A-TRAF6RING, the Kd increased, and binding energy decreased (Figure 9A).
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR titration data shown in Figure 9A.

claim: The drop in binding energy due to E69A substitution (ΔΔGNSB) is 0.82 kcal/mol.
source: The drop in binding energy compared to the wt complex gave the ΔΔGNSB = 0.82 kcal/mol.
evidence: This claim is derived from NMR titration data shown in Figure 9A.

claim: The Kd of R14A-UBC13 with TRAF6RING is 4.29 (±1.71) mM.
source: The titration of R14A-UBC13 with TRAF6RING determined a drop in the binding energy by 1.45 kcal/mol (Figure 9A).
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR titration data shown in Figure 9A.

claim: The contribution of salt-bridge competition in the transient complex (ΔΔGTSB) is 0.63 kcal/mol.
source: Given the value of ΔΔGNSB was determined above, ΔΔGTSB = 0.63 kcal/mol.
evidence: This claim is derived from NMR titration data by subtracting ΔΔGNSB from the total drop in binding energy for R14A-UBC13.

claim: The repulsive effect of E100 on the transient complex (ΔΔGTrep) is 0.24 kcal/mol.
source: Since ΔΔGNSB + ΔΔGTSB = 1.45 kcal/mol, ΔΔGTrep = 0.24 kcal/mol (Equation 1).
evidence: This claim is derived from NMR titration data by subtracting the sum of ΔΔGNSB and ΔΔGTSB from the total ΔΔGd.

claim: RNF38RING can activate UBC13 to synthesize polyubiquitin chains.
source: RNF38RING can activate UBC13 to synthesize polyubiquitin chains (Figure 9B).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro ubiquitination assay data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: RNF38RING fails to activate dUBC13 to synthesize polyubiquitin chains.
source: Similar to TRAF6, the RNF38RING fails to activate dUBC13 (Figure 9B).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro ubiquitination assay data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: The Kd of UBC13/RNF38RING interaction is 0.04 mM.
source: The Kd value of UBC13/RNF38RING interaction was 0.04 mM (Figure 9I).
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR titration data shown in Figure 9I.

claim: The Kd of dUBC13/RNF38RING interaction is 0.24 mM, representing a 6-fold drop in affinity.
source: Fitting of peak shifts against ligand: protein ratio yielded the Kd to be 0.25 mM, which corresponds to a 6-fold drop in affinity.
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR titration data shown in Figure 9I.

claim: R14A substitution reduces the binding energy of the UBC13/RNF38RING complex by 0.6 kcal/mol.
source: The Kd of R14A-UBC13/RNF38RING showed a 2.5-fold increase and reduced binding energy by 0.6 kcal/mol.
evidence: This claim is supported by NMR titration data shown in Figure 9I.

claim: The repulsive effect of E100 on the UBC13/RNF38RING transient complex is 0.5 kcal/mol.
source: Given the salt-bridge competition reduces binding energy by 0.6 kcal/mol, the repulsive effect of E100 on the transient complex is 0.5 kcal/mol.
evidence: This claim is derived from NMR titration data by subtracting the salt-bridge competition effect from the total deamidation effect.

claim: UBC13 and dUBC13 conjugate with donor Ub with similar efficiency.
source: Both the UBC13 and dUBC13 conjugated with the donor Ub with similar efficiency, indicating that deamidation does not hamper E2 ~Ub conjugation (Figure 10A and Figure 10—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro conjugation assay data shown in Figure 10A.

claim: UBC13 ~Ub conjugate binds to TRAF6RZ3 while dUBC13 ~Ub conjugate fails to bind.
source: While UBC13 ~Ub conjugate bound to TRAF6RZ3, dUBC13 ~Ub conjugate failed to do so (Figure 10B and Figure 10—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by affinity pull-down assay data shown in Figure 10B.

claim: UBC13 ~Ub binds to RNF38RING while dUBC13 ~Ub does not.
source: In a similar experiment, UBC13 ~Ub but not dUBC13 ~Ub bound to RNF38RING (Figure 10C).
evidence: This claim is supported by affinity pull-down assay data shown in Figure 10C.

claim: Increasing RNF38RING concentration by five-fold improves the rate of Ub discharge from dUBC13 ~Ub.
source: When the concentration of the RNF38RING was increased by five-fold to compensate for the reduced affinity of dUBC13/RING complex, the rate of Ub discharge improved, which confirmed that the cause of the inefficient discharge is the reduced affinity of dUBC13/RING interaction (Figure 10K and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by discharge assay data shown in Figure 10F and K.

claim: The rate of Ub2 synthesis is rapid for UBC13 but slow for dUBC13.
source: The rate of Ub2 synthesis was rapid for UBC13 but slow for dUBC13 (Figure 10L).
evidence: This claim is supported by Ub2 synthesis kinetics data shown in Figure 10L.

claim: The reaction rate for the dUBC13/RING complex is similar to the rate of UBC13 in the absence of RING.
source: Kinetic analysis indicated that the reaction rate for the dUBC13/RING complex is similar to the rate of UBC13 in the absence of RING (Figure 10M and Figure 10—figure supplement 2), indicating that the catalytic effect of RING is absent in the dUBC13/RING complex.
evidence: This claim is supported by kinetic analysis shown in Figure 10M and Figure 10—figure supplement 2.

claim: Deamidation does not significantly affect the Km of the substrate but drastically affects the Kcat of the reaction.
source: A comparison of the kinetic parameters between UBC13 and dUBC13 indicated that deamidation does not significantly affect the Km of the substrate, but drastically affects the Kcat of the reaction (Figure 10N and Figure 10—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by kinetic parameter analysis shown in Figure 10N.

claim: The Kcat of UBC13 and dUBC13 is similar in the absence of a RING domain.
source: Furthermore, in the absence of a RING domain, the Kcat of UBC13 and dUBC13 is similar, confirming that the catalytic activity of UBC13 is unaffected upon deamidation, similar to the observation of Figure 1C.
evidence: This claim is supported by kinetic analysis comparing UBC13 and dUBC13 without RING domain.

claim: The Kcat of dUBC13 does not increase in the presence of RING, confirming that RING domains fail to activate the dUBC13 ~Ub conjugate.
source: However, unlike UBC13, the Kcat of dUBC13 does not increase in the presence of RING, confirming that RING domains fail to bind and activate the dUBC13 ~Ub conjugate.
evidence: This claim is supported by kinetic analysis shown in Figure 10N.

claim: R14-mediated intermolecular salt-bridges are present in several UBC13/RING complexes.
source: Analysis of all the UBC13/RING (or U-box) structures shows that intermolecular salt-bridges involving R14 are present in several of the UBC13/RING complexes (Figure 9—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is based on structural analysis of multiple UBC13/RING complex structures shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claim: R14A substitution reduced the binding energy of UBC13/ZNRF1RING complex by ~1.2 kcal mol−1 as measured by isothermal titration calorimetry.
source: Binding studies by isothermal titration calorimetry measured that R14A substitution reduced the binding energy of UBC13/ZNRF1RING complex by ~1.2 kcal mol−1 (Behera et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Behera et al., 2018).

claim: R14 appears to be a hotspot at the UBC13/TRAF6RING interface.
source: Altogether, R14 appears to be a hotspot at the UBC13/TRAF6RING interface.
evidence: This claim is based on multiple lines of evidence including hotspot prediction algorithms, binding studies, and structural analysis.

claim: Shigella flexneri secretes a Type III effector called OspI, which functions as a deamidase.
source: To inactivate Nf-κB signaling, Shigella flexneri secretes a Type III effector called OspI, which functions as a deamidase (Sanada et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Sanada et al., 2012).

claim: UBC13 functions with several RING-finger E3s like TRAF6 to synthesize K63-linked poly-Ub chains.
source: The E2 UBC13 functions with several RING-finger E3s like TRAF6 to synthesize K63-linked poly-Ub chains that function to activate DNA repair or immune response (Fukushima et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Fukushima et al., 2007).

claim: UBC13 binds a co-factor MMS2, which maintains the linkage specificity of the poly-Ub chains synthesized by UBC13.
source: Apart from the E3s, UBC13 also binds a co-factor MMS2, which does not activate UBC13 but maintains the linkage specificity of the poly-Ub chains synthesized by UBC13 (Branigan et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Branigan et al., 2015).

claim: The RING-finger/U-box domain stabilizes a catalytic-closed conformation of the flexible E2 ~Ub species and drastically enhances the rate of Ub conjugation to substrates.
source: The RING-finger/U-box domain stabilizes a catalytic-closed conformation of the flexible E2 ~Ub species and drastically enhances the rate of Ub conjugation to substrates (Dou et al., 2012; Plechanovová et al., 2012; Pruneda et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Dou et al., 2012; Plechanovová et al., 2012; Pruneda et al., 2012).

claim: In the early events of interleukin-dependent activation of Nf-κB signaling, UBC13 and TRAF6 function together to synthesize both unanchored polyubiquitin chains and anchored polyubiquitin chains on TRAF6 and its substrate NEMO.
source: In the early events of interleukin-dependent activation of Nf-κB signaling, the Ub-conjugating enzyme UBC13, and the Ub-ligase TRAF6 function together to synthesize both unanchored polyubiquitin chains, and anchored polyubiquitin chains on TRAF6 and its substrate NEMO (Chen, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Chen, 2005).

claim: Polyubiquitin chains synthesized by UBC13/TRAF6 serve as a scaffold to bring together TAK1/2 and IKK kinases, leading to phosphorylation and activation of IKK kinases, IκB degradation and nuclear translocation of transcription factor Nf-κB.
source: These chains serve as a scaffold to bring together TAK1/2 and IKK kinases, eventually leading to phosphorylation and activation of the IKK kinases, IκB degradation and nuclear translocation of transcription factor Nf-κB.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge of the NF-κB signaling pathway.

claim: Ubiquitination reactions of TRAF6 with Q100E-UBC13 show a significant drop in polyubiquitination activity.
source: Ubiquitination reactions of TRAF6 either with UBC13 in the presence of OspI or with mutant Q100E-UBC13 (dUBC13) show a significant drop in polyubiquitination activity (Sanada et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Sanada et al., 2012).

claim: The TRAF6RING interacts with UBC13 and with the donor Ub in the UBC13 ~Ub conjugate.
source: TRAF6RING interacts with UBC13 and with the donor Ub in the UBC13 ~Ub conjugate, while the interaction of ZF domains with donor Ub further stabilized the complex (Middleton et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Middleton et al., 2017).

claim: The interaction of ZF domains with donor Ub further stabilizes the UBC13/TRAF6 complex.
source: TRAF6RING interacts with UBC13 and with the donor Ub in the UBC13 ~Ub conjugate, while the interaction of ZF domains with donor Ub further stabilized the complex (Middleton et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Middleton et al., 2017).

claim: Deamidation of amylin accelerates its aggregation and amyloid formation.
source: Deamidation of amylin accelerates its aggregation and amyloid formation (Dunkelberger et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Dunkelberger et al., 2012).

claim: Crystallins deamidate with age, which promotes aggregation and triggers cataract.
source: Crystallins deamidate with age, which promotes its aggregation to trigger cataract (Pande et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Pande et al., 2015).

claim: Deamidation-induced modulation of transient protein-protein association may explain the tendency of crystallins to aggregate.
source: Deamidation-induced modulation of transient protein-protein association may explain the tendency of these proteins to aggregate.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the findings of this study applied to the context of crystallin aggregation.
